summary:
OpusTerra is a web application accessible directly from any browser on desktop or mobile. Our goal is to act as an Earth system trend detective, using an interactive 3D globe that goes beyond displaying data: it identifies regions shifting in opposite directions, validates statistical reliability, and translates complex phenomena into plain-language insights.

What We Are Developing?
1. An intuitive 3D visualization: A color-coded globe highlighting where variables are increasing or decreasing, while explicitly marking areas with statistically unreliable signals as "Uncertain."
2. Evolutionary Timeline: A temporal control allowing users to explore the planet year by year and observe how long-term trends unfold.
3. Automatic Contrast Detection: Unlike platforms that leave users guessing what to look at, our system automatically searches for and highlights paired regions experiencing opposite changes (e.g., adjacent areas where measurements rise versus fall).
4. Plain-Language Comparisons: When a region pair is selected, a side-by-side panel provides a concise, everyday-language explanation of why these contrasting trajectories are occurring.
details:
OpusTerra — Interactive 3D Earth Observation Explorer

Developed by Team Pegaso-X

OpusTerra is an interactive 3D web application that transforms 24 years of NASA Earth observation data into an accessible visual narrative of long-term climate and ecological trends across Honduras and Central America.

What It Does & How It Works

OpusTerra allows users to explore complete annual environmental data from 2001 to 2024 on a responsive 3D globe:

  • Multi-Variable Analysis: Users can toggle between three core indicators; 2m air temperature, vegetation index (NDVI), and observed/modeled precipitation to inspect statistically significant upward or downward trends.
  • Interactive Timeline & Trend-Pairing: Users can scrub through annual timelines and use a side-by-side comparison mode to contrast nearby zones experiencing opposite environmental trajectories (e.g., localized greening vs. vegetation loss).
  • Decoupled Architecture: Instead of forcing heavy climate computations inside the browser, an automated Python ETL pipeline pre-processes raw NASA satellite and reanalysis datasets into lightweight, static JSON payloads served directly to the web client.

Benefits & Intended Impact

Raw Earth science datasets (NetCDF4/HDF) are typically locked behind specialized GIS software and steep technical barriers. OpusTerra bridges the gap between open NASA science and local action:

  • Democratizing Climate Data: Translates complex gridded satellite metrics into plain-language summaries and intuitive 3D visuals for students, educators, journalists, and local decision makers in Central America.
  • Actionable Regional Insights: Helps communities identify localized environmental vulnerabilities, heat anomalies, and ecosystem shifts without requiring GIS expertise or high-end hardware.

Creativity & User Experience

Rather than relying on static 2D choropleth maps or dense spreadsheets, OpusTerra combines a smooth 3D globe with a "trend-pairing" contrast engine. By visually pairing adjacent areas with diverging ecological paths, spatial anomalies become immediately tangible and intuitive to non-technical audiences.

Scientific Validity & Key Factors Considered

  • Temporal Baseline Integrity: Enforced a strict common monthly baseline (2000-02 to 2025-09) so that only complete 12-month calendar years (2001–2024) are evaluated, eliminating seasonal bias.
  • Spatial & Statistical Rigor: Applied non-parametric trend detection (Mann-Kendall test, Theil-Sen slope estimator) with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction to isolate statistically robust signals, while explicitly distinguishing gridded cell values from area-averaged precipitation metrics.
  • Accessibility & Performance: Built a mobile-first, collapsible UI featuring an integrated glossary and plain-language readouts. Offloading processing to the backend ensures 60fps 3D rendering on standard consumer devices.
  • Responsible Scope: Explicitly framed as an exploratory visualization and educational tool rather than a predictive weather model or an official diagnostic/health alert system.

Tools, Languages & NASA Data

  • NASA Data Sources (GES DISC & Earthdata):
    • MODIS MOD13C2: Monthly Vegetation Index (NDVI).
    • MERRA-2: 2m surface air temperature and flux precipitation reanalysis.
    • GPM IMERG: Multi-satellite observed precipitation.
  • Backend & Data Pipeline: Python (xarray, rioxarray, earthaccess, pydap via OPeNDAP) processing NetCDF4 and GeoTIFF formats.
  • Statistical Methods: Mann-Kendall trend test, Theil-Sen slope estimator, Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction.
  • Frontend & 3D Engine: Svelte 5, TypeScript, Vite, and Three.js.
